tasks.title: Accept the restart recovery contract
tasks.objective: Decide which metadata, replay, and live-control classes can honestly survive daemon restart before selecting a store or changing the runtime.
tasks.outcome: The persistence decision has an accepted, testable recovery boundary with explicit identity, corruption, cleanup, orphan, and unsupported-state semantics.
acceptance: The decision separates durable metadata and replay from live PTY ownership and names every unsupported recovery claim.
Process identity never relies on PID alone and ambiguous adoption fails closed.
Atomicity, corruption, retention, cleanup, daemon epoch, and orphan policy are explicit before implementation.
The selected design uses existing platform or maintained library behavior unless repository evidence proves it insufficient.

verification.proves: The accepted decision defines the supported recovery class and its failure semantics.

tasks.title: Implement and prove the accepted recovery class
tasks.objective: Persist and reconcile only the state accepted by T-001, with real restart evidence and fail-closed stale or corrupt state handling.
tasks.outcome: Daemon restart preserves exactly the declared state without adopting an unrelated process or claiming unsupported live PTY control.
acceptance: A real daemon restart proves every supported metadata, replay, lineage, and control guarantee.
Interrupted or corrupt stored generations select one valid generation or return a typed failure.
Stale or recycled process identity never signals, attaches to, or adopts an unrelated process.
Applicable persistence wrong cases become executable fixtures and global retention remains bounded.

verification.proves: Restart, corruption, stale-identity, retention, and full repository checks pass.
